purpose: Compile-only validation of Aurora's DVD adapter and its nod dependency. No player ISO was present in recomp/input/RM3E01_00, so no disc was opened or read.

provider_compatibility.issue: The nod prebuilt package contains nod_static.lib, but its nodConfig.cmake selects a GNU-style libnod_static.a name when configuring MinGW, so AURORA_NOD_PROVIDER=package cannot find its own x64 archive in this environment.
provider_compatibility.workaround: A local, reviewable CMake provider patch imports the official MinGW-compatible nod_static.lib and nod.dll filenames and declares the documented Windows system libraries. Patch: patches/aurora_nod_mingw_package.patch. No nod binary or upstream nod source was changed.
provider_compatibility.validation: CMake configured with AURORA_NOD_PROVIDER=package and AURORA_NOD_LINKAGE=static using the patched provider, and the aurora_dvd target completed incrementally. The original compilation had already succeeded through a temporary build-only package shim. All 9 nod_* undefined symbols in libaurora_dvd.a were found among the global definitions in nod_static.lib. This is provider/build and symbol-inventory validation, not a final executable link.

limitations: Aurora DVD and nod were not linked into an executable or called at runtime.
No ISO, Wii partition, file path, resource bytes, decryption, or title-specific behavior was tested.
SDL3 libusb remains disabled for this probe; controller adapter support is unvalidated.
